36:13.ar: وَٱضۡرِبۡ لَهُم مَّثَلًا أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةِ إِذۡ جَآءَهَا ٱلۡمُرۡسَلُونَ
36:13.en: And present to them an example: the people of the city, when the messengers came to it

36:14.ar: إِذۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡهِمُ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَعَزَّزۡنَا بِثَالِثࣲ فَقَالُوٓاْ إِنَّآ إِلَيۡكُم مُّرۡسَلُونَ
36:14.en: When We sent to them two but they denied them, so We strengthened them with a third, and they said, "Indeed, we are messengers to you

36:15.ar: قَالُواْ مَآ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا بَشَرࣱ مِّثۡلُنَا وَمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ مِن شَيۡءٍ إِنۡ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا تَكۡذِبُونَ
36:15.en: They said, "You are not but human beings like us, and the Most Merciful has not revealed a thing. You are only telling lies

36:16.ar: قَالُواْ رَبُّنَا يَعۡلَمُ إِنَّآ إِلَيۡكُمۡ لَمُرۡسَلُونَ
36:16.en: They said, "Our Lord knows that we are messengers to you

36:17.en: And we are not responsible except for clear notification

36:18.ar: قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا تَطَيَّرۡنَا بِكُمۡۖ لَئِن لَّمۡ تَنتَهُواْ لَنَرۡجُمَنَّكُمۡ وَلَيَمَسَّنَّكُم مِّنَّا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
36:18.en: They said, "Indeed, we consider you a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and there will surely touch you, from us, a painful punishment

36:19.ar: قَالُواْ طَٰٓئِرُكُم مَّعَكُمۡ أَئِن ذُكِّرۡتُمۚ بَلۡ أَنتُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ مُّسۡرِفُونَ
36:19.en: They said, "Your omen is with yourselves. Is it because you were reminded? Rather, you are a transgressing people

36:20.ar: وَجَآءَ مِنۡ أَقۡصَا ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ رَجُلࣱ يَسۡعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱتَّبِعُواْ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ
36:20.en: And there came from the farthest end of the city a man, running. He said, "O my people, follow the messengers

36:21.ar: ٱتَّبِعُواْ مَن لَّا يَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ أَجۡرࣰ ا وَهُم مُّهۡتَدُونَ
36:21.en: Follow those who do not ask of you [any] payment, and they are [rightly] guided

36:22.ar: وَمَالِيَ لَآ أَعۡبُدُ ٱلَّذِي فَطَرَنِي وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
36:22.en: And why should I not worship He who created me and to whom you will be returned

36:23.ar: ءَأَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ ءَالِهَةً إِن يُرِدۡنِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ بِضُرࣲّ لَّا تُغۡنِ عَنِّي شَفَٰعَتُهُمۡ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يُنقِذُونِ
36:23.en: Should I take other than Him [false] deities [while], if the Most Merciful intends for me some adversity, their intercession will not avail me at all, nor can they save me

36:24.ar: إِنِّيٓ إِذࣰ ا لَّفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينٍ
36:24.en: Indeed, I would then be in manifest error

36:25.en: Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me

36:26.ar: قِيلَ ٱدۡخُلِ ٱلۡجَنَّةَۖ قَالَ يَٰلَيۡتَ قَوۡمِي يَعۡلَمُونَ
36:26.en: It was said, "Enter Paradise." He said, "I wish my people could know

36:27.ar: بِمَا غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمُكۡرَمِينَ
36:27.en: Of how my Lord has forgiven me and placed me among the honored

36:3.en: Indeed you, [O Muhammad], are from among the messengers

36:5.en: [This is] a revelation of the Exalted in Might, the Merciful

36:6.ar: لِتُنذِرَ قَوۡمࣰ ا مَّآ أُنذِرَ ءَابَآؤُهُمۡ فَهُمۡ غَٰفِلُونَ
36:6.en: That you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are unaware

36:7.ar: لَقَدۡ حَقَّ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ عَلَىٰٓ أَكۡثَرِهِمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
36:7.en: Already the word has come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe

36:8.ar: إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَا فِيٓ أَعۡنَٰقِهِمۡ أَغۡلَٰلࣰ ا فَهِيَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَذۡقَانِ فَهُم مُّقۡمَحُونَ
36:8.en: Indeed, We have put shackles on their necks, and they are to their chins, so they are with heads [kept] aloft

36:9.ar: وَجَعَلۡنَا مِنۢ بَيۡنِ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ سَدࣰّ ا وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِمۡ سَدࣰّ ا فَأَغۡشَيۡنَٰهُمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يُبۡصِرُونَ
36:9.en: And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them, so they do not see

36:10.ar: وَسَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَأَنذَرۡتَهُمۡ أَمۡ لَمۡ تُنذِرۡهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
36:10.en: And it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe

36:11.ar: إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلذِّكۡرَ وَخَشِيَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنَ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِۖ فَبَشِّرۡهُ بِمَغۡفِرَةࣲ وَأَجۡرࣲ كَرِيمٍ
36:11.en: You can only warn one who follows the message and fears the Most Merciful unseen. So give him good tidings of forgiveness and noble reward

36:12.ar: إِنَّا نَحۡنُ نُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰ وَنَكۡتُبُ مَا قَدَّمُواْ وَءَاثَٰرَهُمۡۚ وَكُلَّ شَيۡءٍ أَحۡصَيۡنَٰهُ فِيٓ إِمَامࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
36:12.en: Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and record what they have put forth and what they left behind, and all things We have enumerated in a clear register

6:122.ar: أَوَمَن كَانَ مَيۡتࣰ ا فَأَحۡيَيۡنَٰهُ وَجَعَلۡنَا لَهُۥ نُورࣰ ا يَمۡشِي بِهِۦ فِي ٱلنَّاسِ كَمَن مَّثَلُهُۥ فِي ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ لَيۡسَ بِخَارِجࣲ مِّنۡهَاۚ كَذَٰلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
6:122.en: And is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him light by which to walk among the people like one who is in darkness, never to emerge therefrom? Thus it has been made pleasing to the disbelievers that which they were doing

57:16.ar: ۞أَلَمۡ يَأۡنِ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَن تَخۡشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمۡ لِذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا نَزَلَ مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا يَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِن قَبۡلُ فَطَالَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡأَمَدُ فَقَسَتۡ قُلُوبُهُمۡۖ وَكَثِيرࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ فَٰسِقُونَ
57:16.en: Has the time not come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of Allah and what has come down of the truth? And let them not be like those who were given the Scripture before, and a long period passed over them, so their hearts hardened; and many of them are defiantly disobedient

57:17.ar: ٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحۡيِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَاۚ قَدۡ بَيَّنَّا لَكُمُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ
57:17.en: Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its lifelessness. We have made clear to you the signs; perhaps you will understand

18:22.ar: سَيَقُولُونَ ثَلَٰثَةࣱ رَّابِعُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡ وَيَقُولُونَ خَمۡسَةࣱ سَادِسُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡ رَجۡمَۢا بِٱلۡغَيۡبِۖ وَيَقُولُونَ سَبۡعَةࣱ وَثَامِنُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡۚ قُل رَّبِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ بِعِدَّتِهِم مَّا يَعۡلَمُهُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣱۗ فَلَا تُمَارِ فِيهِمۡ إِلَّا مِرَآءࣰ ظَٰهِرࣰ ا وَلَا تَسۡتَفۡتِ فِيهِم مِّنۡهُمۡ أَحَدࣰ ا
18:22.en: They will say there were three, the fourth of them being their dog; and they will say there were five, the sixth of them being their dog - guessing at the unseen; and they will say there were seven, and the eighth of them was their dog. Say, [O Muhammad], "My Lord is most knowing of their number. None knows them except a few. So do not argue about them except with an obvious argument and do not inquire about them among [the speculators] from anyone

106:1.en: For the accustomed security of the Quraysh

17:90.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ تَفۡجُرَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَنۢبُوعًا
17:90.en: And they say, "We will not believe you until you break open for us from the ground a spring

17:91.ar: أَوۡ تَكُونَ لَكَ جَنَّةࣱ مِّن نَّخِيلࣲ وَعِنَبࣲ فَتُفَجِّرَ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرَ خِلَٰلَهَا تَفۡجِيرًا
17:91.en: Or [until] you have a garden of palm tress and grapes and make rivers gush forth within them in force [and abundance]

17:92.ar: أَوۡ تُسۡقِطَ ٱلسَّمَآءَ كَمَا زَعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡنَا كِسَفًا أَوۡ تَأۡتِيَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ قَبِيلًا
17:92.en: Or you make the heaven fall upon us in fragments as you have claimed or you bring Allah and the angels before [us]

17:93.ar: أَوۡ يَكُونَ لَكَ بَيۡتࣱ مِّن زُخۡرُفٍ أَوۡ تَرۡقَىٰ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَلَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لِرُقِيِّكَ حَتَّىٰ تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيۡنَا كِتَٰبࣰ ا نَّقۡرَؤُهُۥۗ قُلۡ سُبۡحَانَ رَبِّي هَلۡ كُنتُ إِلَّا بَشَرࣰ ا رَّسُولࣰ ا
17:93.en: Or you have a house of gold or you ascend into the sky. And [even then], we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book we may read." Say, "Exalted is my Lord! Was I ever but a human messenger

16:48.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ مِن شَيۡءࣲ يَتَفَيَّؤُاْ ظِلَٰلُهُۥ عَنِ ٱلۡيَمِينِ وَٱلشَّمَآئِلِ سُجَّدࣰ ا لِّلَّهِ وَهُمۡ دَٰخِرُونَ
16:48.en: Have they not considered what things Allah has created? Their shadows incline to the right and to the left, prostrating to Allah, while they are humble

29:20.ar: قُلۡ سِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ بَدَأَ ٱلۡخَلۡقَۚ ثُمَّ ٱللَّهُ يُنشِئُ ٱلنَّشۡأَةَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
29:20.en: Say, [O Muhammad], "Travel through the land and observe how He began creation. Then Allah will produce the final creation. Indeed Allah, over all things, is competent

30:20.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَنۡ خَلَقَكُم مِّن تُرَابࣲ ثُمَّ إِذَآ أَنتُم بَشَرࣱ تَنتَشِرُونَ
30:20.en: And of His signs is that He created you from dust; then, suddenly you were human beings dispersing [throughout the earth]

7:131.ar: فَإِذَا جَآءَتۡهُمُ ٱلۡحَسَنَةُ قَالُواْ لَنَا هَٰذِهِۦۖ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ سَيِّئَةࣱ يَطَّيَّرُواْ بِمُوسَىٰ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥٓۗ أَلَآ إِنَّمَا طَٰٓئِرُهُمۡ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
7:131.en: But when good came to them, they said, "This is ours [by right]." And if a bad [condition] struck them, they saw an evil omen in Moses and those with him. Unquestionably, their fortune is with Allah, but most of them do not know

28:20.ar: وَجَآءَ رَجُلࣱ مِّنۡ أَقۡصَا ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ يَسۡعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱلۡمَلَأَ يَأۡتَمِرُونَ بِكَ لِيَقۡتُلُوكَ فَٱخۡرُجۡ إِنِّي لَكَ مِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ
28:20.en: And a man came from the farthest end of the city, running. He said, "O Moses, indeed the eminent ones are conferring over you [intending] to kill you, so leave [the city]; indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisors

5:105.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَنفُسَكُمۡۖ لَا يَضُرُّكُم مَّن ضَلَّ إِذَا ٱهۡتَدَيۡتُمۡۚ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
5:105.en: O you who have believed, upon you is [responsibility for] yourselves. Those who have gone astray will not harm you when you have been guided. To Allah is you return all together; then He will inform you of what you used to do

34:47.ar: قُلۡ مَا سَأَلۡتُكُم مِّنۡ أَجۡرࣲ فَهُوَ لَكُمۡۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ شَهِيدࣱ‏
34:47.en: Say, "Whatever payment I might have asked of you - it is yours. My payment is only from Allah, and He is, over all things, Witness

KetIP_ve9ww.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Yasin, the Believer of the Town (36:13-27)
KetIP_ve9ww.one_line: The story of the believer in Surat Yasin: real life comes through obedience and calling to Allah, against superstition, apathy and paid religion.
KetIP_ve9ww.summary: The only story in Surat Yasin is the man who came running from the far end of the town, so it carries the surah's meaning: real life is the life of the soul, gained by obeying Allah and calling others to Him, while the heedless are the living dead. He warns against chasing details Allah left out, like the town's location. The people demanded miracles because familiarity blinded them to the wonders around them, including their own bodies. Their reply, 'we see an evil omen in you', leads him into a long critique of superstition: omens, misused istikharah, horoscopes and the inflation of jinn, magic and the evil eye that grows when a civilisation declines. Istikharah is for two equal options you have not yet decided between, not for waiting on signs. The believer's word 'ya qawmi' shows belonging and responsibility: even with three messengers present, he felt the religion was his to carry. Every Muslim either carries the concern of the deen or is a burden on it. 'Follow those who ask no wage' leads to a warning that money corrupts dawah, citing the great imams who took nothing. Killed, the man's first words were wishing his people knew, so his memory lives on while they are forgotten.

outline.heading: The only story in the surah carries its meaning
outline.gist: When a surah holds one story found nowhere else, read it with extra care because the surah's axis turns on it.

outline.heading: Obedience through dawah is what gives life
outline.gist: Yasin, within the section from Al-Ahzab to Az-Zumar on submission, defines life as more than biology: animals breathe and eat as we do.

outline.heading: Souls die and Allah revives them
outline.gist: A soul starved of Allah's love and of calling to Him dies, but as Allah revives the earth He revives hearts.

outline.heading: The heedless are the living dead
outline.gist: The opening of the surah describes ghaflah: the one who does not care at all, unreachable by any call.

outline.heading: Do not dwell on what Allah left out
outline.gist: The town's location is unknown and useless; like the number of the cave sleepers, such debates waste time.

outline.heading: Three messengers in one town
outline.gist: They declared openly that they were messengers and were called liars.

outline.heading: Demanding miracles out of over-familiarity
outline.gist: People seek the extraordinary because they stopped seeing the wonder in the ordinary; maturity means stepping back to see it.

outline.heading: The Quran points to signs already before you
outline.gist: Quraysh demanded springs and palaces; the Quran answered with creation, the shade and the origin of man.

outline.heading: The miracle of a single bodily function
outline.gist: A doctor can spend 25 years just understanding the kidneys; knowing this keeps you grateful.

outline.heading: The messengers restate their mission
outline.gist: Our duty is only clear delivery; this setup is needed to understand what the believer did.

outline.heading: Reciting 36:18-19 and full assimilation of nun
outline.gist: In 'la'in lam' the nun disappears completely into the lam.

outline.heading: What tatayyur is
outline.gist: Judging reality by something unrelated to it, like taking a stumble on the way to an interview as a sign.

outline.heading: Istikharah: only between two equal options
outline.gist: It is not for choosing between obedience and sin or for decisions already made; it declares to Allah that you want what brings you closer.

outline.heading: No waiting for signs after istikharah
outline.gist: The companions decided and relied on Allah; a flat tyre is a nail, not a message.

outline.heading: Declining civilisations sink into superstition
outline.gist: Muslims have inflated jinn, magic and the evil eye until no failure is ever our own fault.

outline.heading: Scapegoating as a tool to silence
outline.gist: Said to Musa, Nuh and others, and used in media today to stir hatred; then threats replace discussion.

outline.heading: 'Your omen is with you'
outline.gist: The messengers turned the omen back on the people themselves.

outline.heading: Israf: excess in everything
outline.gist: Excess is not only in money but in war, defiance and rejection; mothers still blame a bride for misfortune.

outline.heading: Muslims judge by evidence: no contagion, no omens
outline.gist: The Prophet rejected omens and loved optimism; even educated people now follow horoscopes.

outline.heading: Islam took us out of darkness; why return to it?
outline.gist: These people were dead in mind, rejecting messengers who called them to good.

outline.heading: Reciting 36:20-22
outline.gist: A man came running from the farthest part of the city.

outline.heading: Why 'from the farthest part' comes first
outline.gist: Word order stresses how far he came, unlike the similar verse in the story of Musa.

MAEZinoDHWk.title: Tafseer of Surat ar-Rahman: The Final Verses
MAEZinoDHWk.one_line: Concluding ar-Rahman: gratitude as Islamic maturity, the lower pair of gardens, hearts purified of jealousy, and the last man to leave Hell.
MAEZinoDHWk.summary: He recaps the cluster of surahs from Qaf to al-Hadid as a series of choices and presents ar-Rahman's choice as gratitude versus losing one's blessings, asked again and again by its refrain. Humans quickly take blessings for granted, so he defines Islamic maturity as growing sensitivity to what Allah has given, which shapes how one prays and speaks to Him. Our debt is infinite, but like an athlete trailing badly we should still give our best, because Allah answers excellence with His own. Turning to verses 62 onward, he reads the second pair of gardens as a rank slightly below the first, matching the Quran's three groups. No one in Paradise resents a higher rank, because jealousy and arrogance rest on illusions that are stripped away before entry, illustrated by Abdullah ibn Rawahah's slightly lower rank after a moment's hesitation at Mu'tah. Life, he says, is either gratitude or perseverance. He compares the wording of the two descriptions, from dark green foliage to gushing springs, then the fruits, exclusive spouses and incomparable furnishings. The hadith of the last man to leave Hell shows insatiable human desire, which should be redirected toward Paradise through a selfless path. The surah ends with the blessed name of the Lord, and its unanswered question will return as the record we write.

outline.heading: The short, comprehensive surahs
outline.gist: The final quarter is short yet comprehensive and focused on values and principles rather than rulings, ideal for those who struggle to memorize.

outline.heading: The cluster of choices
outline.gist: From Qaf onward each surah sets a choice: righteousness, purpose, guidance, knowledge over whims, and use of blessings.

outline.heading: Ar-Rahman: gratitude or loss
outline.gist: The refrain asks over thirty times which favours we deny; the first and greatest blessing is that our Lord is ar-Rahman.

outline.heading: We take blessings for granted
outline.gist: Humans stop noticing whatever is always there, which is why children seldom appreciate their parents' provision; zooming out has to be taught.

outline.heading: Blessings everyone shares
outline.gist: The surah lists universal blessings: being made from clay, the two seas, ships that float, even death and accountability.

outline.heading: Islamic maturity is sensitivity to blessings
outline.gist: Maturity is seeing ever more of what one has been given; prayer and khushu reflect how one views Allah's generosity.

outline.heading: You could have been anything
outline.gist: We had no say in being created as we are and own nothing to object with; revelation and intellect are given so life is worth living.

outline.heading: An infinite debt and the athlete's grit
outline.gist: We cannot repay Allah and have often walked the opposite way, but like a player ten goals down we keep giving our best.

outline.heading: Even Hell is a blessing
outline.gist: That oppressors and abusers cannot escape justice is itself a mercy.

outline.heading: Recap: two gardens and the reward of excellence
outline.gist: Those who fear standing before their Lord receive two gardens meeting every desire; give Allah your best and see His best.

outline.heading: Answering a question: whose excellence comes first
outline.gist: An attendee suggests Allah has already shown His excellence and now awaits ours; he accepts it as an equally profound reading.

outline.heading: 'Besides these, two more gardens'
outline.gist: Read as one degree below; the Quran regularly divides people into three groups, two of whom succeed.

outline.heading: No jealousy or arrogance enters Paradise
outline.gist: Diseases of the heart must be purified first; jealousy rests on illusions that vanish when one sees Hell brought forth on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Certainty and love for those ranked higher
outline.gist: Everyone's iman becomes certain when experienced directly; seeing someone ranked higher by Allah brings love, not resentment.

outline.heading: Abdullah ibn Rawahah's moment of hesitation
outline.gist: The Prophet described Zayd, Ja'far and Ibn Rawahah in Paradise, the last slightly lower for an inner hesitation at Mu'tah no one else saw; every detail is weighed.

outline.heading: Life is gratitude or perseverance
outline.gist: Use what you have in service, or persevere toward what you lack; picture perseverance as climbing a mountain at night in wind and rain.

outline.heading: Dark green gardens
outline.gist: Where the first gardens have many branches, these are so green they look black: abundant options, less sharply defined.

outline.heading: Gushing springs versus flowing ones
outline.gist: Flowing water is more peaceful than gushing water; the word choices mark the difference in rank.

outline.heading: Grateful even for what we dislike
outline.gist: The alternative to everything is nothingness, humanity's deepest fear; even death is a blessing that motivates action.

outline.heading: Recitation note: elongation counts
outline.gist: The six-count madd followed by two counts for the doubled nun when pausing.

outline.heading: Fruits, palms and pomegranates
outline.gist: Naming a few fruits signals plenty but less variety than the first gardens; the repeated question keeps pressing for an answer.

outline.heading: Good and beautiful companions in pavilions
outline.gist: Exclusive intimacy answers the human need to be wanted by one person; it applies to both men and women.

outline.heading: Answering a question on jinn and the companions
outline.gist: He understands these as beings Allah creates in Paradise for its people, not humans made the object of others' pleasure.

outline.heading: Green cushions and incomparable carpets
outline.gist: Abqari describes something unmatched, hence its use for a genius; the furnishings exceed anything imagined.

outline.heading: The last man to leave Hell
outline.gist: Restored in the river of life, he asks for one tree, then a better one, then another, each time promising to ask for no more.

outline.heading: The black hole of desire
outline.gist: Wanting more is human and not wrong, but worldly consumption only deepens the emptiness, which is why the well-off reach for pills.

outline.heading: Be selfish for Paradise by being selfless here
outline.gist: The only way to satisfy that ultimate selfishness is a path of selflessness, compassion and responsibility for others.

outline.heading: Ten times the greatest kingdom
outline.gist: Finding Paradise full, he is offered the dominion of the greatest king and then tenfold, and that is the lowest rank.

outline.heading: The highest see their Lord
outline.gist: The highest ranks care only for meeting Allah, the source of all beauty, which they do twice a day.

outline.heading: Blessed is the name of your Lord
outline.gist: The surah begins with the name ar-Rahman and ends with His blessed name as the source of all barakah.

outline.heading: The unanswered question returns
outline.gist: The refrain fades without an answer but will return on the Day of Judgment, answered by the record we write now.

2:143.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ أُمَّةࣰ وَسَطࣰ ا لِّتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ شَهِيدࣰ اۗ وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡقِبۡلَةَ ٱلَّتِي كُنتَ عَلَيۡهَآ إِلَّا لِنَعۡلَمَ مَن يَتَّبِعُ ٱلرَّسُولَ مِمَّن يَنقَلِبُ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيۡهِۚ وَإِن كَانَتۡ لَكَبِيرَةً إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَى ٱللَّهُۗ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَٰنَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِٱلنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
2:143.en: And thus we have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you. And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels. And indeed, it is difficult except for those whom Allah has guided. And never would Allah have caused you to lose your faith. Indeed Allah is, to the people, Kind and Merciful

2:275.en: Those who consume interest cannot stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity. That is because they say, "Trade is [just] like interest." But Allah has permitted trade and has forbidden interest. So whoever has received an admonition from his Lord and desists may have what is past, and his affair rests with Allah. But whoever returns to [dealing in interest or usury] - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide eternally therein

9:37.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلنَّسِيٓءُ زِيَادَةࣱ فِي ٱلۡكُفۡرِۖ يُضَلُّ بِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يُحِلُّونَهُۥ عَامࣰ ا وَيُحَرِّمُونَهُۥ عَامࣰ ا لِّيُوَاطِـُٔواْ عِدَّةَ مَا حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ فَيُحِلُّواْ مَا حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُۚ زُيِّنَ لَهُمۡ سُوٓءُ أَعۡمَٰلِهِمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
9:37.en: Indeed, the postponing [of restriction within sacred months] is an increase in disbelief by which those who have disbelieved are led [further] astray. They make it lawful one year and unlawful another year to correspond to the number made unlawful by Allah and [thus] make lawful what Allah has made unlawful. Made pleasing to them is the evil of their deeds; and Allah does not guide the disbelieving people

7:32.ar: قُلۡ مَنۡ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَخۡرَجَ لِعِبَادِهِۦ وَٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ مِنَ ٱلرِّزۡقِۚ قُلۡ هِيَ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا خَالِصَةࣰ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۗ كَذَٰلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لِقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡلَمُونَ
7:32.en: Say, "Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has produced for His servants and the good [lawful] things of provision?" Say, "They are for those who believe during the worldly life [but] exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection." Thus do We detail the verses for a people who know

7:33.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ رَبِّيَ ٱلۡفَوَٰحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنۡهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ وَٱلۡإِثۡمَ وَٱلۡبَغۡيَ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَأَن تُشۡرِكُواْ بِٱللَّهِ مَا لَمۡ يُنَزِّلۡ بِهِۦ سُلۡطَٰنࣰ ا وَأَن تَقُولُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
7:33.en: Say, "My Lord has only forbidden immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed - and sin, and oppression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has not sent down authority, and that you say about Allah that which you do not know

VgrN0B1lcwk.speaker: adnan
VgrN0B1lcwk.speaker_note: 12th in his 'Achieving the Balance' series, speaks of his own fatwa caution and the 'haram police'
VgrN0B1lcwk.title: Achieving the Balance: Haram and Halal
VgrN0B1lcwk.one_line: Making haram halal is a grave wrong, but making halal haram is just as bad, and scholars say worse: it cheapens the real red lines.
VgrN0B1lcwk.summary: Opening with the verse against saying with your tongues 'this is halal and this is haram', the twelfth balance khutbah starts with the agreed part: Allah set boundaries, and turning the forbidden into the permitted ruins faith and community. A key role of Islamic education is to make those lines clear, as the Prophet said to do what he commands as far as you can but never cross what he forbids. He names two forces pushing the line today: normalization, where crossing once without visible consequence makes it routine, as with riba and the Arabs shifting the sacred months; and weakness, since the weak adopt the values of the strong. Haram means sacred, like the Sacred Mosque. Then the balance: making halal haram is equally wrong, and scholars considered it worse, citing the verse asking who forbade Allah's adornments. Overextending the list of prohibitions makes the next generation stop respecting all of them, as when a parent equates a haircut with drinking. He criticizes the 'haram police', checking every ingredient, and the history of banning TV, satellite dishes and the internet. Personal caution in grey areas is admirable but cannot be imposed on a community, since only Allah prohibits and the default is permissibility.

outline.heading: The twelfth balance
outline.gist: Liars against Allah do not succeed. Each talk in the series states something undisputed and then the piece needed to balance it, so that we become the nation of moderation Allah described.

outline.heading: Never make haram halal
outline.gist: Moderation needs exceptions and context; the definite part today is that turning the forbidden into the permitted can ruin faith, communities and the identity Allah gave us.

outline.heading: Has Allah given you permission?
outline.gist: Did Allah authorize you to declare things forbidden or allowed, or are you inventing as you go, and what do inventors expect on the Day of Judgment?

outline.heading: Make Allah's boundaries clear
outline.gist: A core function of Islamic institutions and education is making every Muslim clear on what is haram; the Prophet said to do what he commands as far as you can but never cross what he forbids.

outline.heading: Whoever crosses Allah's limits wrongs himself
outline.gist: Those who cross His boundaries and act as if they were not there wrong themselves and face painful punishment; no two Muslims dispute that Allah drew red lines.

outline.heading: Lawful by the word of Allah; a Muslim's sanctity
outline.gist: Spouses become lawful to each other only through Allah's word in a valid marriage, and every aspect of a fellow Muslim, his life, wealth and honour, is sacred.

outline.heading: Pushing the line
outline.gist: People nudge the line left and right: how haram can it be if everyone does it or the country has legalized it? He gives two reasons.

outline.heading: Reason one: normalization
outline.gist: Cross a red line once, nothing happens, so you cross it again until it feels normal and is hard to undo; those who consume riba end up saying trade is the same as riba.

outline.heading: Shifting the sacred months
outline.gist: The Arabs moved Muharram around to suit their wars; tampering with what Allah made sacred is an increase in disbelief.

outline.heading: Reason two: the weak adopt the values of the strong
outline.gist: Muslims today are weaker scientifically, academically and in numbers, so they feel they must take on others' values to seem civilized and progressive, just as others once took on Muslim values when Muslims were strong.

outline.heading: Haram means sacred
outline.gist: Killing and stealing are not up for debate; haram means sacred, as in al-Masjid al-Haram, a line you have no permission to cross.

outline.heading: The agreed part, in Arabic
outline.gist: He restates the first half in Arabic.

outline.heading: Making halal haram is just as bad
outline.gist: Forbidding the lawful is equally wrong and causes as many problems; scholars of merit consider it worse.

outline.heading: Who forbade Allah's adornment?
outline.gist: The Quran asks who dares forbid the adornment and good things Allah brought out for people, which are for believers and disbelievers in this life and for believers alone on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Allah forbade specific things
outline.gist: Allah listed what He forbade, including speaking about Him without knowledge; calling things haram to be safe does not protect Islam.

outline.heading: A hundred red lines, respected by none
outline.gist: Turn a list of ten sacred lines into a hundred and people stop respecting all of them, becoming a leading reason people leave the faith.

outline.heading: A haircut is not alcohol
outline.gist: Telling a son a haircut you dislike is as haram as drinking or zina pushes him to do both; do not add culture, tradition or personal preference to what Allah forbade.

outline.heading: The haram police
outline.gist: Being extra careful in your own life is admirable, but you cannot force it on others or call things haram that are not; only Allah has that authority.

outline.heading: The default is permissibility
outline.gist: He thinks long before calling anything haram, since he would be prohibiting on Allah's behalf; the origin of everything is permissibility, and only specific things are forbidden.

outline.heading: The grey area
outline.gist: Between clear halal and clear haram are matters many do not know but scholars do; if you cannot ask, play it safe yourself, but do not stop someone who researched it.

outline.heading: Stop reading every ingredient
outline.gist: Skip the marshmallows with gelatin, but stop hunting through every label; it belittles the real prohibitions such as associating partners with Allah and indecency.

outline.heading: Zina is not an Oreo
outline.gist: Sexual relations outside marriage are an absolute line that cannot be equated with eating an Oreo; on lesser matters, go to people of knowledge and hear more than one opinion.

outline.heading: Raise children to know the real lines
outline.gist: Adding a million false prohibitions leaves him unable to protect the real ones; raise children to know exactly where the lines are and keep culture out of it.

outline.heading: Personal caution versus communal rulings
outline.gist: Avoiding something over a difference of opinion is godly, but communities cannot be held to it; he lived through internet, satellite dishes, TV and computers each being declared haram.

outline.heading: Every sheikh now has all four
outline.gist: Rushing to prohibit makes people disrespect the word haram; once a real line is crossed the way back is hard, so protect the lines by not adding to them.

outline.heading: Worse, but slower to show
outline.gist: Both errors are the same in their nature, and forbidding the lawful is worse; its consequences just take another generation to appear. He then restates the balance in Arabic.

outline.heading: The balance, in Arabic
outline.gist: He continues the restatement in Arabic.

outline.heading: Both errors are equally wrong
outline.gist: Permitting the forbidden and forbidding the permitted are equally wrong; his job is to keep reminding people of the real boundaries, which gets harder as more is added.

outline.heading: Second khutbah in Arabic
outline.gist: The second khutbah, given in Arabic.

2:143.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ أُمَّةࣰ وَسَطࣰ ا لِّتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ شَهِيدࣰ اۗ وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡقِبۡلَةَ ٱلَّتِي كُنتَ عَلَيۡهَآ إِلَّا لِنَعۡلَمَ مَن يَتَّبِعُ ٱلرَّسُولَ مِمَّن يَنقَلِبُ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيۡهِۚ وَإِن كَانَتۡ لَكَبِيرَةً إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَى ٱللَّهُۗ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَٰنَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِٱلنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
2:143.en: And thus we have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you. And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels. And indeed, it is difficult except for those whom Allah has guided. And never would Allah have caused you to lose your faith. Indeed Allah is, to the people, Kind and Merciful

2:111.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَن يَدۡخُلَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ إِلَّا مَن كَانَ هُودًا أَوۡ نَصَٰرَىٰۗ تِلۡكَ أَمَانِيُّهُمۡۗ قُلۡ هَاتُواْ بُرۡهَٰنَكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:111.en: And they say, "None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian." That is [merely] their wishful thinking, Say, "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful

43:81.ar: قُلۡ إِن كَانَ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ وَلَدࣱ فَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلۡعَٰبِدِينَ
43:81.en: Say, [O Muhammad], "If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of [his] worshippers

53:23.ar: إِنۡ هِيَ إِلَّآ أَسۡمَآءࣱ سَمَّيۡتُمُوهَآ أَنتُمۡ وَءَابَآؤُكُم مَّآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَا مِن سُلۡطَٰنٍۚ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّ وَمَا تَهۡوَى ٱلۡأَنفُسُۖ وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَهُم مِّن رَّبِّهِمُ ٱلۡهُدَىٰٓ
53:23.en: They are not but [mere] names you have named them - you and your forefathers - for which Allah has sent down no authority. They follow not except assumption and what [their] souls desire, and there has already come to them from their Lord guidance

53:28.ar: وَمَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنۡ عِلۡمٍۖ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّۖ وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّنَّ لَا يُغۡنِي مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا
53:28.en: And they have thereof no knowledge. They follow not except assumption, and indeed, assumption avails not against the truth at all

22:46.ar: أَفَلَمۡ يَسِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَتَكُونَ لَهُمۡ قُلُوبࣱ يَعۡقِلُونَ بِهَآ أَوۡ ءَاذَانࣱ يَسۡمَعُونَ بِهَاۖ فَإِنَّهَا لَا تَعۡمَى ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرُ وَلَٰكِن تَعۡمَى ٱلۡقُلُوبُ ٱلَّتِي فِي ٱلصُّدُورِ
22:46.en: So have they not traveled through the earth and have hearts by which to reason and ears by which to hear? For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts

7:179.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ذَرَأۡنَا لِجَهَنَّمَ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِۖ لَهُمۡ قُلُوبࣱ لَّا يَفۡقَهُونَ بِهَا وَلَهُمۡ أَعۡيُنࣱ لَّا يُبۡصِرُونَ بِهَا وَلَهُمۡ ءَاذَانࣱ لَّا يَسۡمَعُونَ بِهَآۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ كَٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ بَلۡ هُمۡ أَضَلُّۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡغَٰفِلُونَ
7:179.en: And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. Those are like livestock; rather, they are more astray. It is they who are the heedless

3:31.en: Say, [O Muhammad], "If you should love Allah, then follow me, [so] Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful

5:54.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَن يَرۡتَدَّ مِنكُمۡ عَن دِينِهِۦ فَسَوۡفَ يَأۡتِي ٱللَّهُ بِقَوۡمࣲ يُحِبُّهُمۡ وَيُحِبُّونَهُۥٓ أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ يُجَٰهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا يَخَافُونَ لَوۡمَةَ لَآئِمࣲۚ ذَٰلِكَ فَضۡلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤۡتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ
5:54.en: O you who have believed, whoever of you should revert from his religion - Allah will bring forth [in place of them] a people He will love and who will love Him [who are] humble toward the believers, powerful against the disbelievers; they strive in the cause of Allah and do not fear the blame of a critic. That is the favor of Allah; He bestows it upon whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing

39:23.ar: ٱللَّهُ نَزَّلَ أَحۡسَنَ ٱلۡحَدِيثِ كِتَٰبࣰ ا مُّتَشَٰبِهࣰ ا مَّثَانِيَ تَقۡشَعِرُّ مِنۡهُ جُلُودُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخۡشَوۡنَ رَبَّهُمۡ ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمۡ وَقُلُوبُهُمۡ إِلَىٰ ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُدَى ٱللَّهِ يَهۡدِي بِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَمَن يُضۡلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنۡ هَادٍ
39:23.en: Allah has sent down the best statement: a consistent Book wherein is reiteration. The skins shiver therefrom of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts relax at the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills. And one whom Allah leaves astray - for him there is no guide

fcZmDzgi34M.title: Achieving the Balance: The Intellect and the Heart
fcZmDzgi34M.one_line: Islam is built on reason and evidence, but faith held only in the mind rusts; the heart must follow the intellect into love and tears.
fcZmDzgi34M.summary: This balance khutbah first establishes the undisputed point: Islam is a religion of logic and evidence. The Quran repeatedly demands proof from its opponents, calls idols mere names with no authority, says assumption is no substitute for truth, and ends verse after verse urging reflection. Tawhid is the simplest explanation of existence, and the Arabs rejected it not because it made no sense but because it ended corruption and profit; a person of tawhid becomes dangerous to anything irrational. Blindness is of hearts, not eyes, and people who do not use their minds are worse than cattle. Even a mistaken jurist is rewarded for sound reasoning, and superstition and amulets were removed so the community could think. The balance: no one can sustain faith with the intellect alone. Without the heart, belief slowly rusts. He cites the sweetness of faith found in loving Allah and His Prophet most, the companions' tears, Hanzala fearing he was a hypocrite, Abu Bakr weeping too much to lead prayer, and the verse about skins shivering at the Quran. He apologizes that speakers like him often fail to reach hearts, warns that emotion-only faith is a ticking bomb, and notes the companions remembered the feeling more than the words.

outline.heading: A religion of reason

outline.heading: Bring your proof
outline.gist: The Quran keeps telling opponents to bring their evidence, even saying that if the Most Merciful had a son, the Prophet would be the first to worship.

outline.heading: Names you made up
outline.gist: Idols are names invented by people and their forefathers with no authority; they follow assumption and desire, and assumption is no substitute for the truth.

outline.heading: So that you may reflect
outline.gist: Verse after verse ends hoping we will reflect and understand, because people easily follow beliefs that make no sense; tawhid is the simplest concept there is.

outline.heading: Tawhid explains everything
outline.gist: One source explains why everything works the same way from the atom to the galaxy; the Arabs rejected it not because it made no sense but because it closed the doors to corruption.

outline.heading: Tawhid isn't lucrative
outline.gist: Without idols, clergy could not sell rulings or control people; a servant of Allah alone becomes dangerous, refusing anything irrational or corrupt.

outline.heading: Hearts go blind, not eyes
outline.gist: It is the inner faculty that goes blind, not the eyes; the world is full of people who cannot see yet have insight.

outline.heading: Worse than cattle
outline.gist: Those with minds, eyes and ears they never use are like livestock or worse, since cattle have no choice; there is no cure for indifference. Look at what you were created from and at your food.

outline.heading: The mistaken jurist is still rewarded
outline.gist: A jurist who reaches the right ruling gets two rewards and a wrong one gets one, because his reasoning was sound; sound logic cannot be faulted.

outline.heading: Superstition was removed
outline.gist: Charms, fairy tales and carrying objects for protection were abolished, because a community rises only when it starts thinking properly.

outline.heading: The agreed part, in Arabic
outline.gist: He calls this point undisputed and restates it in Arabic.

outline.heading: The mind cannot carry faith alone
outline.gist: No Muslim can continue the journey with only the intellect invested; you believe because it is the simplest explanation, but the heart must be at the same level.

outline.heading: Without the heart, belief rusts
outline.gist: Belief settled by the mind slowly rusts and fades if the heart does not come along; if you love Allah, follow the Prophet, and Allah will bring a people He loves and who love Him.

outline.heading: The sweetness of faith
outline.gist: Three things bring it: loving Allah and His Prophet above all, loving others only for Allah, and hating to leave the faith as one hates being thrown into fire.

outline.heading: Eyes filled with tears
outline.gist: Companions report again and again that when the Prophet admonished them their eyes flowed and their hearts trembled.

outline.heading: Hanzala: 'I have become a hypocrite'
outline.gist: Hanzala lost the feeling at home among his family and animals and feared hypocrisy; Abu Bakr felt the same. Their hearts were moved because the mind had already settled, so the two agreed without forcing tears.

outline.heading: Emotion-only faith collapses
outline.gist: Faith entered only through emotion, without understanding, comes crashing down when the winds blow; it must start with the intellect, and then the heart must follow.

outline.heading: An apology from speakers
outline.gist: He apologizes for himself and other speakers who offer the intellect without the heart, so people come and go unchanged and no closer to Allah.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr weeping and Umar's two lines
outline.gist: Aisha asked that Abu Bakr not lead the prayer because he sobbed through Al-Fatiha; Umar, who could line everyone up at once, had two lines on his face from crying at night.

outline.heading: Skins that shiver at the best speech
outline.gist: Allah sent down the best speech, consistent and repeated, at which the skins of those who fear their Lord shiver.

outline.heading: Search for your heart
outline.gist: Skins and hearts then soften into Allah's remembrance, but only once the mind has full clarity; then look for where your heart is, find the missing piece and fix it.

outline.heading: Muslims are meant to be in love
outline.gist: Listening to the Quran should be the best time of your week; people in love talk only of the one they love, and Muslims should be in love with Allah, the Prophet and the Book.

outline.heading: They remembered the feeling, not the words
outline.gist: Faith on emotion alone is a ticking bomb, but hearts filled with love remember how it felt: the companions kept few of his exact words and wept for those days, and we remember the feeling of Ramadan nights, not the surahs.

outline.heading: Second khutbah in Arabic
outline.gist: After noting that this cannot change unless the mind leads the way, he continues in Arabic for the rest of the khutbah.

36:13.ar: وَٱضۡرِبۡ لَهُم مَّثَلًا أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةِ إِذۡ جَآءَهَا ٱلۡمُرۡسَلُونَ
36:13.en: And present to them an example: the people of the city, when the messengers came to it

36:14.ar: إِذۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡهِمُ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَعَزَّزۡنَا بِثَالِثࣲ فَقَالُوٓاْ إِنَّآ إِلَيۡكُم مُّرۡسَلُونَ
36:14.en: When We sent to them two but they denied them, so We strengthened them with a third, and they said, "Indeed, we are messengers to you

36:15.ar: قَالُواْ مَآ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا بَشَرࣱ مِّثۡلُنَا وَمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ مِن شَيۡءٍ إِنۡ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا تَكۡذِبُونَ
36:15.en: They said, "You are not but human beings like us, and the Most Merciful has not revealed a thing. You are only telling lies

36:16.ar: قَالُواْ رَبُّنَا يَعۡلَمُ إِنَّآ إِلَيۡكُمۡ لَمُرۡسَلُونَ
36:16.en: They said, "Our Lord knows that we are messengers to you

36:17.en: And we are not responsible except for clear notification

36:18.ar: قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا تَطَيَّرۡنَا بِكُمۡۖ لَئِن لَّمۡ تَنتَهُواْ لَنَرۡجُمَنَّكُمۡ وَلَيَمَسَّنَّكُم مِّنَّا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
36:18.en: They said, "Indeed, we consider you a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and there will surely touch you, from us, a painful punishment

36:19.ar: قَالُواْ طَٰٓئِرُكُم مَّعَكُمۡ أَئِن ذُكِّرۡتُمۚ بَلۡ أَنتُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ مُّسۡرِفُونَ
36:19.en: They said, "Your omen is with yourselves. Is it because you were reminded? Rather, you are a transgressing people

36:20.ar: وَجَآءَ مِنۡ أَقۡصَا ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ رَجُلࣱ يَسۡعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱتَّبِعُواْ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ
36:20.en: And there came from the farthest end of the city a man, running. He said, "O my people, follow the messengers

36:21.ar: ٱتَّبِعُواْ مَن لَّا يَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ أَجۡرࣰ ا وَهُم مُّهۡتَدُونَ
36:21.en: Follow those who do not ask of you [any] payment, and they are [rightly] guided

36:22.ar: وَمَالِيَ لَآ أَعۡبُدُ ٱلَّذِي فَطَرَنِي وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
36:22.en: And why should I not worship He who created me and to whom you will be returned

36:23.ar: ءَأَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ ءَالِهَةً إِن يُرِدۡنِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ بِضُرࣲّ لَّا تُغۡنِ عَنِّي شَفَٰعَتُهُمۡ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يُنقِذُونِ
36:23.en: Should I take other than Him [false] deities [while], if the Most Merciful intends for me some adversity, their intercession will not avail me at all, nor can they save me

36:24.ar: إِنِّيٓ إِذࣰ ا لَّفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينٍ
36:24.en: Indeed, I would then be in manifest error

36:25.en: Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me

36:26.ar: قِيلَ ٱدۡخُلِ ٱلۡجَنَّةَۖ قَالَ يَٰلَيۡتَ قَوۡمِي يَعۡلَمُونَ
36:26.en: It was said, "Enter Paradise." He said, "I wish my people could know

36:27.ar: بِمَا غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمُكۡرَمِينَ
36:27.en: Of how my Lord has forgiven me and placed me among the honored

36:28.ar: ۞وَمَآ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ مِن جُندࣲ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا كُنَّا مُنزِلِينَ
36:28.en: And We did not send down upon his people after him any soldiers from the heaven, nor would We have done so

36:29.ar: إِن كَانَتۡ إِلَّا صَيۡحَةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ فَإِذَا هُمۡ خَٰمِدُونَ
36:29.en: It was not but one shout, and immediately they were extinguished

36:30.ar: يَٰحَسۡرَةً عَلَى ٱلۡعِبَادِۚ مَا يَأۡتِيهِم مِّن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا كَانُواْ بِهِۦ يَسۡتَهۡزِءُونَ
36:30.en: How regretful for the servants. There did not come to them any messenger except that they used to ridicule him

36:31.ar: أَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ كَمۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا قَبۡلَهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡقُرُونِ أَنَّهُمۡ إِلَيۡهِمۡ لَا يَرۡجِعُونَ
36:31.en: Have they not considered how many generations We destroyed before them - that they to them will not return

36:32.ar: وَإِن كُلࣱّ لَّمَّا جَمِيعࣱ لَّدَيۡنَا مُحۡضَرُونَ
36:32.en: And indeed, all of them will yet be brought present before Us

36:6.ar: لِتُنذِرَ قَوۡمࣰ ا مَّآ أُنذِرَ ءَابَآؤُهُمۡ فَهُمۡ غَٰفِلُونَ
36:6.en: That you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are unaware

36:7.ar: لَقَدۡ حَقَّ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ عَلَىٰٓ أَكۡثَرِهِمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
36:7.en: Already the word has come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe

36:8.ar: إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَا فِيٓ أَعۡنَٰقِهِمۡ أَغۡلَٰلࣰ ا فَهِيَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَذۡقَانِ فَهُم مُّقۡمَحُونَ
36:8.en: Indeed, We have put shackles on their necks, and they are to their chins, so they are with heads [kept] aloft

36:9.ar: وَجَعَلۡنَا مِنۢ بَيۡنِ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ سَدࣰّ ا وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِمۡ سَدࣰّ ا فَأَغۡشَيۡنَٰهُمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يُبۡصِرُونَ
36:9.en: And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them, so they do not see

36:10.ar: وَسَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَأَنذَرۡتَهُمۡ أَمۡ لَمۡ تُنذِرۡهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
36:10.en: And it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe

21:92.ar: إِنَّ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أُمَّتُكُمۡ أُمَّةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ وَأَنَا۠ رَبُّكُمۡ فَٱعۡبُدُونِ
21:92.en: Indeed this, your religion, is one religion, and I am your Lord, so worship Me

23:52.ar: وَإِنَّ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أُمَّتُكُمۡ أُمَّةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ وَأَنَا۠ رَبُّكُمۡ فَٱتَّقُونِ
23:52.en: And indeed this, your religion, is one religion, and I am your Lord, so fear Me

8:25.ar: وَٱتَّقُواْ فِتۡنَةࣰ لَّا تُصِيبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مِنكُمۡ خَآصَّةࣰۖ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
8:25.en: And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively, and know that Allah is severe in penalty

3:196.ar: لَا يَغُرَّنَّكَ تَقَلُّبُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فِي ٱلۡبِلَٰدِ
3:196.en: Be not deceived by the [uninhibited] movement of the disbelievers throughout the land

3:197.ar: مَتَٰعࣱ قَلِيلࣱ ثُمَّ مَأۡوَىٰهُمۡ جَهَنَّمُۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمِهَادُ
3:197.en: [It is but] a small enjoyment; then their [final] refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place

62:2.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي بَعَثَ فِي ٱلۡأُمِّيِّـۧنَ رَسُولࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَيُزَكِّيهِمۡ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَإِن كَانُواْ مِن قَبۡلُ لَفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
62:2.en: It is He who has sent among the unlettered a Messenger from themselves reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book and wisdom - although they were before in clear error

6:10.ar: وَلَقَدِ ٱسۡتُهۡزِئَ بِرُسُلࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِكَ فَحَاقَ بِٱلَّذِينَ سَخِرُواْ مِنۡهُم مَّا كَانُواْ بِهِۦ يَسۡتَهۡزِءُونَ
6:10.en: And already were messengers ridiculed before you, but those who mocked them were enveloped by that which they used to ridicule

19:85.ar: يَوۡمَ نَحۡشُرُ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ إِلَى ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ وَفۡدࣰ ا
19:85.en: On the Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation

19:86.ar: وَنَسُوقُ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ وِرۡدࣰ ا
19:86.en: And will drive the criminals to Hell in thirst

39:71.ar: وَسِيقَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ زُمَرًاۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءُوهَا فُتِحَتۡ أَبۡوَٰبُهَا وَقَالَ لَهُمۡ خَزَنَتُهَآ أَلَمۡ يَأۡتِكُمۡ رُسُلࣱ مِّنكُمۡ يَتۡلُونَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّكُمۡ وَيُنذِرُونَكُمۡ لِقَآءَ يَوۡمِكُمۡ هَٰذَاۚ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِنۡ حَقَّتۡ كَلِمَةُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ عَلَى ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
39:71.en: And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups until, when they reach it, its gates are opened and its keepers will say, "Did there not come to you messengers from yourselves, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?" They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers

39:72.ar: قِيلَ ٱدۡخُلُوٓاْ أَبۡوَٰبَ جَهَنَّمَ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۖ فَبِئۡسَ مَثۡوَى ٱلۡمُتَكَبِّرِينَ
39:72.en: [To them] it will be said, "Enter the gates of Hell to abide eternally therein, and wretched is the residence of the arrogant

39:73.ar: وَسِيقَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوۡاْ رَبَّهُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡجَنَّةِ زُمَرًاۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءُوهَا وَفُتِحَتۡ أَبۡوَٰبُهَا وَقَالَ لَهُمۡ خَزَنَتُهَا سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيۡكُمۡ طِبۡتُمۡ فَٱدۡخُلُوهَا خَٰلِدِينَ
39:73.en: But those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups until, when they reach it while its gates have been opened and its keepers say, "Peace be upon you; you have become pure; so enter it to abide eternally therein," [they will enter]

BX6k1DRDaes.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Yasin, the Believer's Living Heart and 'Alas for the Servants' (36:28-32)
BX6k1DRDaes.one_line: The believer of Yasin shows real life is a heart alive with love of Allah and of guiding others; heedless nations fall to one cry.
BX6k1DRDaes.summary: Surat Yasin defines real life as obeying Allah and calling others to Him, not wealth or status. He points to the emptiness of modern life, shown by the antidepressant market in wealthy countries, while stressing that people who need treatment should seek it. The believer who ran from the far end of the town is a proof against us: three prophets were already there, he lived far away, and he was killed, yet his first wish was that his people could know. Love of others' guidance is the measure of a Muslim, and withdrawing into a private religiosity is a disease of the heart: the ship hadith and the angel told to begin destruction with a worshipper who never grew angry for Allah show that being good is not enough without reforming. The town needed no army, only one cry, so do not fear the many. He asks for effort and patience in conveying the guidance you were given, while recognising few would do what that man did. 'Alas for the servants' laments humans who need guidance more than any creature yet mock those who bring it because it exposes their hidden diseases. The pleasure-seeker loses both worlds, while one whose heart is full of love for Allah is at peace anywhere. All will be brought before Allah, none absent.

outline.heading: Real life is obedience and calling others to Allah
outline.gist: Yasin's theme is the life of the soul and a good memory with Allah after death, not biological functions, wealth or power.

outline.heading: The emptiness that kills
outline.gist: People spend their lives looking for meaning and eventually have to ask why they exist and whether their life pleases Allah.

outline.heading: The tranquillity of the obedient believer
outline.gist: One who obeys and calls to Allah has a peace nothing outside can disturb, without fear of age, poverty or illness.

outline.heading: Money cannot buy that peace
outline.gist: Doctors see wealthy, successful people in deep distress; the scale is visible in the market value of antidepressants.

outline.heading: A different emptiness in comfortable societies
outline.gist: Treatment matters for those who need it, but the highest use is in developed countries where material needs are met, pointing to an inner void only obedience fills.

outline.heading: Three prophets and a backward, violent people
outline.gist: The town called its messengers a bad omen and threatened to kill them; the believer of Yasin is a proof against all of us.

outline.heading: Violence betrays a weak argument

outline.heading: Effort and patience, not martyrdom

outline.heading: Human power is fragile

outline.heading: A few such believers would change a city

outline.heading: Those sent to help are rejected or killed

outline.heading: Humans need guidance more than any creature
outline.gist: A foal walks in minutes; a human needs years of care, and children make a parent cowardly and miserly, as the saying goes.

outline.heading: Following every desire is not a way of life
outline.gist: Without messengers who teach the Book, wisdom and purification, people would destroy each other like animals fighting over food.

outline.heading: Why messengers are mocked
outline.gist: They point to the pride, showing off, envy, stinginess and lust inside us that we do not want to hear about.

outline.heading: A doctor colleague: 'then why live?'
outline.gist: Hearing he did not drink or womanise, a colleague asked what the point of his life was; pitiable is one who limits life to those things.

outline.heading: What you would not want for your child is probably wrong
outline.gist: People who drink do not want it for their children; you do not need a sheikh to tell you.

outline.heading: Generations destroyed before them
outline.gist: Civilisations like the pharaohs, whose pyramids still puzzle researchers, were destroyed and never returned.

outline.heading: The pleasure-seeker is not happier
outline.gist: It is not this world for him and the next for you: he loses both, left with fleeting pleasure and lasting harm like a damaged liver.

outline.heading: A heart full of Allah's love is content anywhere
outline.gist: In the masjid or at home he has peace and gains both worlds.

outline.heading: Lamma, not lam: it has not yet happened
outline.gist: Every word of the verse is needed; lamma means not yet but expected.

outline.heading: All together, in Our presence
outline.gist: Jami' means one place and one time, and 'ladayna' means gathered by Allah's will, not by their choosing.

outline.heading: Brought in person, none absent
outline.gist: No one sends a substitute as Abu Lahab did in battle; not one in a billion is missed. The question is how you will be brought.

outline.heading: Prayer to reach the believer's station
outline.gist: He asks Allah to place love of Him and His religion in our hearts as He did in the believer of Yasin's.

ASNa7PFmAe4.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Waqi'ah, Part 1: Verses 1-19
ASNa7PFmAe4.one_line: Al-Waqi'ah 1-19: the inevitable Event reshuffles all status, strips everything physical away, and sorts people into three groups.
ASNa7PFmAe4.summary: Al-Waqi'ah continues the cluster of surahs that pose life's biggest choices, asking which of three groups you want to be in on the Day of Judgment. The Event is described in the past tense because to Allah it has as good as happened, and no one can deny it. It lowers and raises: worldly status built on wealth, lineage, colour, titles and fame is reshuffled, the arrogant are raised the size of ants, and value is judged by what was in the heart. The earth is violently shaken and mountains crumble to scattered dust, so nothing physical is left: no home, possessions, phone or supplier, as the pandemic's empty shelves hinted. Only the inner self remains, and deeds take form beside their owner. People become three groups: the fortunate, the wretched and the forerunners brought near, many from earlier generations but few from later ones. He links that to the Prophet's warning that he feared abundance of this world, not poverty, for his ummah, and to wealth used without gratitude. The odds of two good groups out of three favour us, but the decisive choices come quietly, without any dramatic music, and can be made right now. He closes with the forerunners' jewelled couches, immortal youths serving them and drink without headache, urging people to serve in this life and to remember the choice is theirs.

outline.heading: A beloved surah in a cluster of life's big choices
outline.gist: The surahs from Qaf onward each pose a question: righteousness or falsehood, purpose or aimlessness, gratitude or ingratitude; Al-Waqi'ah asks which of three people you will be.

outline.heading: A simple surah that begins and ends with three groups
outline.gist: One of the most straightforward themes in the Quran; he then recites the opening.

outline.heading: Al-Waqi'ah: the reality that falls into place
outline.gist: Waqi' is reality as it is; the Event slowly tilts toward the moment it lands and becomes the only thing that is.

outline.heading: The future told in the past tense
outline.gist: Allah speaks of what will happen as if it already has, because His word needs no waiting.

outline.heading: No soul can deny its occurrence
outline.gist: Believe it or not, protest or not, it is coming; figure out where you will be.

outline.heading: This world's measures of status
outline.gist: Background, wealth, education, politics, gender, colour all feed a complicated metric of who is high and low.

outline.heading: It lowers and raises: the metric changes
outline.gist: Lineage, looks, bank balance and the letters around your name stop mattering; there are only three slots.

outline.heading: The arrogant raised the size of ants
outline.gist: People who had crowds waiting for them will be trampled; fame is not evil, but it is not where value comes from.

outline.heading: Judged by what was in the heart
outline.gist: Intentions, hopes, selflessness, trustworthiness and honesty are all that will be weighed.

outline.heading: Resurrected unable even to cover yourself
outline.gist: No connections or workarounds remain; only merit in Allah's eyes.

outline.heading: The mask ripped away
outline.gist: The image we build is torn off and we stand exposed if there was no substance behind it.

outline.heading: Bounties we can never repay
outline.gist: Sight, hearing, safety from war and dictators have no price; all that is left is dedicating your life to pleasing Him.

outline.heading: Iqlab: noon becomes meem before ba
outline.gist: A tajweed note on the small meem above the noon.

outline.heading: The earth shaken violently
outline.gist: Rajj is shaking to the point of breaking; the verbal noun after the verb signals it happens to the fullest extent.

outline.heading: Mountains crumbled to pieces
outline.gist: Bass is crumbling into small bits; the world as we know it is gone.

outline.heading: Nothing physical is left
outline.gist: No home, clothes, phone or store; like children who think chickens come from Costco, we assumed supplies were endless until the pandemic's empty shelves.

outline.heading: Scattered dust and nowhere to go
outline.gist: Haba' munbath is particles too fine to gather; no call to make, no bus to wait for, as hard to grasp as infinity.

outline.heading: Only what is inside remains
outline.gist: Everything we use to cover who we are is removed; deeds and morals take physical form and follow their owner.

outline.heading: What is left of you?
outline.gist: Allah looks at hearts and deeds, not bodies; titles and possessions are erased, so work on why you do what you do.

outline.heading: Three groups: the bottom line of the human story
outline.gist: A very long, complex story ends in three groups of humans and jinn, and each of us must work out which we will be in.

outline.heading: The fortunate, the wretched and the forerunners
outline.gist: The rhetorical question builds desire for the first and dread of the second; repeating 'the forerunners' says words cannot describe them.

outline.heading: Brought near: many from the early, few from the later
outline.gist: Thullah is a share by percentage; the earlier nations supplied a larger share of the forerunners.

outline.heading: Pioneers who refuse mediocrity
outline.gist: A companion prayed to be among the few, since few servants are grateful; forerunners saw the opportunity and chose to excel.

outline.heading: Two out of three: the odds are in your favour
outline.gist: Only one group is a problem; just make sure you are not in the third.

outline.heading: Big decisions come without background music
outline.gist: Life has no dramatic soundtrack; many decisive choices are already made and another can be made right now, seen only by you and Allah.

outline.heading: Our appointment is at the Basin
outline.gist: Too busy to accept invitations, the Prophet told companions to meet him at the Hawd, where some will be called near and others turned away.

outline.heading: Why fewer from the later: 'I do not fear poverty for you'
outline.gist: When wealth came from Bahrain, the Prophet told the poor he feared abundance of this world would ruin them as it ruined those before.

outline.heading: Too much and too little gratitude
outline.gist: The rich who give everywhere outrank others, as the poor companions learned when the wealthy copied their dhikr; with great wealth comes great responsibility.

outline.heading: Jewelled couches facing one another
outline.gist: Thrones studded with gems; the forerunners recline in the company of the great names they only read about.

outline.heading: Immortal youths serve them
outline.gist: Learn to serve in this world so that you are served in the next; the servants are ever-young and eager.

outline.heading: Drink without headache or intoxication
outline.gist: What you gave up in this world for Allah is returned better and lasting, with no price at the end.

outline.heading: Your group is your choice
outline.gist: Read the coming verses, especially the third page; this is not predestined against you, Allah gave you the choice.
